chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee', from Salih ibn Uqbah, from Bashir al-Dahhan, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Sometimes I miss the Hajj, so I spend the Day of 'Arafah at the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him).' He said, 'Well done, O Bashir! Any believer who visits the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), acknowledging his right, on a day other than an Eid or the Day of 'Arafah, Allah will record for him twenty purified and accepted Hajj, twenty accepted 'Umrah, and twenty battles fought with a Messenger Prophet or a Just Imam.'
And whoever visits him on an Eid day... and the hadith continues in its full length.

key_terms.عَرَفَةَ: The Day of 'Arafah (9th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting Imam Husain's grave instead of performing Hajj?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) distinguishes this specific reward from the general virtue of Ziyarah by excluding the days of Eid and 'Arafah, thereby emphasizing the unique spiritual merit of visiting Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) on ordinary days. This hadith, recorded in Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, underscores the concept of *Tawassul* through the Ahl al-Bayt, positioning the shrine as a locus of divine grace where a single visit accrues the cumulative rewards of multiple pilgrimages and military expeditions with the Prophets.
